    Track 2 · Hands-on · Lesson 8

    Merge the adapter, run inference, ship an artifact

    After this lesson you can merge a LoRA adapter into the base, save and reload a standalone fine-tuned model, run inference on it, and know what export formats exist for deployment.

    Level: intermediate Read time: ~8 min Prerequisites: Evaluate by hand: run the gold set, compute the metric Verified: 13 Nov 2026

    You have a fine-tuned adapter that beats the baseline. To use it in production you have two choices, both covered in Track 1: keep the base + adapter separate (handy for serving many tasks off one base), or merge the adapter into the weights to get a single standalone model. This lesson does the merge and ships an artifact.

    Merge the adapter into the base

    merge_and_unload folds the LoRA adapter's learned change directly into the base weights and returns an ordinary model with no adapter and no runtime overhead. Load the base in fp32 for the merge, even if you trained on a bf16 base. The LoRA update is small next to the weights it is added to, and bf16 keeps only about three significant digits, so adding in bf16 rounds part of the update away. Merging is a one-off, so the CPU and fp32 are fine; you cast down once, afterwards.

    Before you merge, record what the unmerged model (base + adapter) answers on a few gold prompts. After merging, the same prompts should give the same answers. That five-prompt check catches a wrong adapter path, a mismatched base or a broken merge before anything ships.

    import json, torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from peft import PeftModel

model_id = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct"
use_bf16 = torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(including_emulation=False)
use_fp16 = torch.cuda.is_available() and not use_bf16
dtype = torch.bfloat16 if use_bf16 else (torch.float16 if use_fp16 else torch.float32)   # Lesson 2.1, for the reload
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("sft-out/adapter")
base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.float32)   # merge in fp32
tuned = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, "sft-out/adapter")

@torch.no_grad()
def answer(model, prompt):
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
    text = tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
    out = model.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=8, do_sample=False)
    return tok.decode(out[0][ids["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True).strip()

with open("gold.jsonl") as f:                 # Lesson 2.3's gold set
    probe = [json.loads(line)["prompt"] for line in f][:5]
before = [answer(tuned, p) for p in probe]     # base + adapter, not merged

merged = tuned.merge_and_unload()      # a plain AutoModelForCausalLM, no PEFT wrapper
after = [answer(merged, p) for p in probe]
print(sum(x == y for x, y in zip(before, after)), "of", len(probe), "answers match")   # expect 5 of 5

    Save it as a standalone model

    save_pretrained writes the weights in safetensors — the safe, fast default format — plus the config. Cast to bf16 first: SmolLM2 itself ships in bf16, and it halves the file. Save the tokenizer alongside so the folder is self-contained.

    merged = merged.to(torch.bfloat16)           # cast once, after the fp32 merge
merged.save_pretrained("sft-out/merged")     # model.safetensors + config.json
tok.save_pretrained("sft-out/merged")        # tokenizer files

import os
print(os.listdir("sft-out/merged"))

    Reload and run — no peft needed

    The merged folder is a normal model. Loading it requires only transformers; there's no adapter to attach.

    m = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("sft-out/merged", dtype=dtype)
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("sft-out/merged")

msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Classify the sentiment as positive or negative: I would buy it again."}]
text = t.apply_chat_template(msgs, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
ids = t(text, return_tensors="pt")
print(t.decode(m.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=8, do_sample=False)[0][ids["input_ids"].shape[1]:],
               skip_special_tokens=True).strip())

    Merge vs keep separate

    Merge when you'll deploy this one task — simplest to serve, zero adapter overhead. Keep the adapter separate when you serve many tasks off one shared base — swap a few-megabyte adapter instead of loading a whole model per task.

    Export formats for deployment

    The safetensors folder runs anywhere transformers (or vLLM) runs — great for a GPU server. For edge / CPU deployment you'll often convert to GGUF (the llama.cpp format) and quantize, so the model runs efficiently on a laptop or phone. The conversion is a separate step with llama.cpp's tooling: its convert_hf_to_gguf.py script reads the merged folder (for example with --outtype q8_0), and Lesson 4.6 covers the quantization choices. We have not run that step for this lesson, so check llama.cpp's README for the current command. The key point is that your merged model is the starting artifact for any of these paths, and the five-prompt check above is worth repeating on whatever file you produce. (BrewSLM automates export to GGUF, ONNX, TensorRT, Hugging Face and Docker formats, and vLLM is one of its serving options rather than an export format — Track 3.)

    You've now done the entire by-hand pipeline: environment, model, data, tokenization, LoRA training, evaluation, and shipping. The next lesson, the capstone, stitches it into one script you can run start-to-finish.

    Recap

    • merge_and_unload folds the adapter into the weights: one plain model, no peft at inference.
    • Merge in fp32, cast down once afterwards, and check that the merged answers match the unmerged ones.
    • The safetensors folder is the starting point for every export path: GGUF, ONNX, TensorRT or straight to a GPU server.

    Try it (5 minutes)

    Compare the sizes of sft-out/adapter/adapter_model.safetensors and sft-out/merged/model.safetensors (ls -lh). Work out both from the parameter counts before you look.

    Show answer

    The adapter is 921,600 parameters stored in fp32: 921,600 × 4 B ≈ 3.7 MB. The merged model is all 134.5M parameters in bf16: ≈ 269 MB (the tied embedding is stored once). That ratio is why serving many tasks from one base with swappable adapters is cheap, and why a merged model is the simpler thing to ship for one task.

    Key terms

    merge_and_unload
    Folds the LoRA adapter into the base weights, returning a standalone model.
    safetensors
    The safe, fast default weight format save_pretrained writes.
    save_pretrained / from_pretrained
    Write / load a self-contained model + config (+ tokenizer).
    standalone model
    A merged model that needs no adapter at inference.
    GGUF
    The llama.cpp format for efficient CPU/edge inference (a separate conversion step).
